<USER_REQUEST>
hi 



SENTINEL-X — COMPLETE ENTIRE CLI INTEGRATION WITH ANTIGRAVITY AND GIT
Objective
Integrate the official Entire CLI (https://entire.io, official repository: https://github.com/entireio/cli) with my existing SENTINEL-X project so that Entire can capture Antigravity coding sessions, associate AI-assisted changes with Git commits, and preserve searchable development history and checkpoints.
The project is SENTINEL-X Phase 7/8, containing:
agent/ — AI patch planner and generation pipeline.
backend/ — FastAPI application, approvals, workflow, database, and evidence.
frontend/ — React, TypeScript, and Vite dashboard.
verification/ — isolated Docker verification engine, protected tests, patch validation, and evaluator.
scripts/, docs/, README files, and existing integration reports.
The objective is to add Entire to the developer workflow without breaking the existing application, Git workflow, Antigravity configuration, or security controls.
Important: Entire is a development-session provenance and Git-checkpoint tool. It is not the SENTINEL-X runtime verifier, and it must not replace or modify the AI planner, approval workflow, Docker sandbox, verification evaluator, or persisted application evidence.
Do not start over or rebuild the project.
PHASE 1 — INSPECT THE ENVIRONMENT
Before making changes:
Identify the actual SENTINEL-X workspace root.
Determine whether it is the real Git repository or merely an extracted archive.
Run git status --short --branch, git rev-parse --show-toplevel, git remote -v, and inspect the current branch.
Identify existing local modifications, untracked files, ignored files, Git hooks, and core.hooksPath.
Inspect existing Antigravity hook configuration and any other agent integrations.
Check whether the entire CLI is installed, its version, and whether its executable is available through PATH.
Inspect the installed CLI's actual entire --help, entire enable --help, entire status, and relevant agent-management commands.
Inspect existing .entire/ configuration, if present.
Determine whether the current Git remote is shared, public, or private when that information is available. Do not assume repository privacy.
Identify whether this is the shared team repository or a personal clone.
Do not infer Git history from the ZIP archive. If the current workspace lacks .git, locate the real existing repository if available. Do not initialize a new repository or create a new remote without my explicit authorization.
Produce a short preflight report before applying changes.
PHASE 2 — INSTALL THE OFFICIAL ENTIRE CLI
Use only the official Entire CLI from the official project.
Official resources:
Website: [https://entire.io](https://entire.io/)
Source and documentation: [https://github.com/entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli)
Security and privacy documentation: [https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/security-and-privacy.md](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/security-and-privacy.md)
Check the current official installation instructions for the operating system in use.
Requirements:
Prefer the stable release.
Do not install nightly or an unofficial fork.
Check whether an existing installation can be reused before installing another copy.
Verify the installed executable and version.
Do not silently replace another binary or alter unrelated PATH entries.
Do not use elevated privileges unless genuinely required.
Inspect installation commands before executing remote installer scripts.
If installation requires an unavailable permission or an interactive confirmation, stop and give me the exact command to run.
If the official CLI is already installed, do not reinstall it unnecessarily.
PHASE 3 — ENABLE ENTIRE FOR ANTIGRAVITY
Use the official supported Antigravity integration.
First inspect the current CLI's supported commands and agent name. Then configure the repository using the equivalent of:
entire enable --agent antigravity
For initial setup, prefer a local-only checkpoint-sync configuration, equivalent to:
entire enable --agent antigravity --skip-push-sessions
Use these flags only if the installed CLI confirms they are supported.
This initial configuration must not automatically push AI session transcripts or checkpoint data to a remote until the repository privacy and storage destination have been reviewed.
Requirements:
Enable the Antigravity-specific hooks.
Install the necessary Git integration using Entire's supported commands.
Verify the repository's Entire settings.
Verify that Antigravity's hook configuration is correctly installed.
Preserve existing Antigravity settings, hooks, MCP configuration, and agent instructions.
Merge configuration safely rather than overwriting existing JSON or other settings.
Inspect any machine-global configuration changes made by the Entire Antigravity integration.
Back up existing configuration before a necessary modification.
Keep local credentials and private settings out of committed project files.
Confirm that the hook configuration does not disable existing project tools or security restrictions.
Do not use --force unless the current hook installation has been inspected and a reinstall is demonstrably necessary.
Do not manually invent Entire hook formats when the CLI can generate them.
PHASE 4 — PROTECT THE SENTINEL-X REPOSITORY
Before enabling session capture, review the project's tracked and untracked files.
The project includes security-sensitive configuration and runtime artifacts. Pay particular attention to:
.env and all real environment files.
backend/config files containing secrets.
Operator tokens and session credentials.
Neatlogs or other service keys.
SQLite databases and evidence artifacts.
local-audit/ output.
Temporary generated patches and private proposal artifacts.
Docker logs and test reports.
Local caches and virtual environments.
Private model output and diagnostic logs.
Ensure .gitignore excludes the appropriate secrets and generated runtime artifacts without accidentally excluding legitimate source code or required test fixtures.
Do not print secrets or copy them into Entire configuration.
Do not delete or rewrite user data merely to make the repository clean.
Check whether any sensitive files are already tracked. If they are, report the exact file paths without revealing their contents. Do not rewrite Git history, remove tracked files, or rotate credentials without my authorization.
PHASE 5 — REVIEW ENTIRE PRIVACY AND CHECKPOINT STORAGE
Entire can capture prompts, agent transcripts, tool interactions, file changes, and metadata. Its redaction is best-effort and must not be treated as a guarantee.
Read the official security and privacy documentation and inspect the actual available redaction settings.
Verify:
Where session transcripts are stored.
Which Git refs or branches hold checkpoint data.
Whether checkpoint pushing is enabled.
Which remote would receive the checkpoint data.
How session data is redacted.
Which Antigravity integration settings are installed globally.
Whether existing local settings and hooks are preserved.
Whether private source material, credentials, or personal information could enter captured transcripts.
Keep the official secret-redaction mechanisms enabled.
If supported by the installed version, configure additional custom redaction for project-specific credentials or identifiers only when the patterns can be defined safely and accurately.
Do not enable optional PII or external privacy-filter services without explaining the implications and obtaining authorization where needed.
Do not assume screenshots, pasted images, binary data, low-entropy secrets, or arbitrary log output are fully protected by text redaction.
Do not claim the repository is safe for public checkpoint publishing merely because the CLI has redaction enabled.
PHASE 6 — CONFIGURE CHECKPOINT STORAGE CORRECTLY
Inspect the current Entire checkpoint backend and synchronization settings.
The intended behavior is:
Keep normal SENTINEL-X source commits on the existing team branch.
Keep Entire checkpoint metadata in the supported separate checkpoint storage mechanism.
Preserve the normal Git history and existing team workflow.
Avoid committing raw AI transcripts directly into application source directories.
Avoid pushing private session metadata to an unapproved remote.
Initially, keep automatic checkpoint pushing disabled until the checkpoint destination is approved.
Then report the recommended configuration options:
Option A — Local-only Entire: Capture and manage checkpoints locally without automatically pushing session data.
Option B — Separate private checkpoint repository: Configure a dedicated private checkpoint destination using the officially supported Entire CLI option, only after its URL, permissions, and privacy have been approved.
Do not create a repository, change Git remotes, grant permissions, or push any checkpoint data without explicit authorization.
If a separate checkpoint repository is approved, configure the actual supported provider and repository syntax rather than inventing a custom format.
Confirm that normal application commits and Entire checkpoint storage remain separate according to the installed CLI's supported design.
PHASE 7 — VERIFY ANTIGRAVITY SESSION CAPTURE
After enabling Entire, validate the integration.
Run the available diagnostic commands, including where supported:
entire version
entire status
entire agent list
entire doctor
git status --short --branch
git config --get core.hooksPath
Use the exact commands supported by the installed release.
Inspect:
Entire's repository enablement status.
Antigravity agent-hook installation.
Git hook installation and chaining.
Configuration validity.
Checkpoint storage configuration.
Local diagnostic output.
Existing project hooks and their continued availability.
Check that the installation does not bypass or suppress existing pre-commit, commit-message, or pre-push checks.
Do not fabricate a captured session or a successful checkpoint.
If the integration requires starting a new Antigravity session, tell me exactly how to do that and how to verify that Entire is recording it.
PHASE 8 — VERIFY CHECKPOINT LINKAGE WITHOUT UNAUTHORIZED COMMITS
Entire links captured session context to Git commits according to its supported workflow.
Do not create a dummy application commit merely to demonstrate that integration.
Do not stage or commit my existing uncommitted changes.
Instead:
Verify the hooks and configuration are installed.
Verify Entire reports the correct repository and agent status.
Verify that the current session can be recognized using supported status or session commands.
Inspect the available checkpoint and session commands.
Explain how a future normal user-created commit will be associated with its Entire checkpoint.
Provide commands for inspecting checkpoint history and recovering a previous session.
If an existing eligible commit/checkpoint is available, inspect it read-only where possible.
Clearly distinguish between verified hook installation and a fully proven commit-to-checkpoint round trip.
A complete round-trip proof may require me to create an ordinary commit in a subsequent Antigravity session. Do not create that commit on my behalf.
PHASE 9 — PRESERVE SENTINEL-X RUNTIME AND VERIFIER INTEGRITY
Entire integration must remain independent of the runtime security architecture.
Do not modify these components just to add Entire:
agent/planner.py
agent/generator.py
backend/workflow.py
backend/approvals.py
backend/services/verification_adapter.py
verification/adapter.py
verification/patch_validator.py
verification/runner.py
verification/evaluator.py
Protected verification tests.
Frontend API contracts and approval semantics.
Do not add Entire checkpoint data to the runtime verification evidence schema unless there is a separately approved, documented requirement. Entire's session history is development provenance, not proof that a patch passed protected tests.
Do not allow Entire hooks to bypass approval, patch validation, Docker sandbox restrictions, or protected-test integrity.
Do not add a new API endpoint, database table, dashboard page, or external runtime service unless I separately authorize that work.
PHASE 10 — DOCUMENT THE INTEGRATION
Add a concise section to the project README or create docs/ENTIRE_INTEGRATION.md.
Document:
What Entire does in SENTINEL-X.
What Entire does not do.
Official installation instructions for supported operating systems.
The correct command to enable Antigravity.
Required Git and CLI prerequisites.
Repository and checkpoint configuration.
Privacy and redaction limitations.
How to inspect status and diagnose hook problems.
How to inspect sessions and checkpoints.
How to resume a supported session.
How to disable Entire safely.
How to configure a separate private checkpoint repository after approval.
How to verify that existing SENTINEL-X runtime behavior remains unchanged.
Use actual commands confirmed against the installed CLI version.
Do not include private tokens, session transcripts, or internal credentials in documentation.
PHASE 11 — REGRESSION AND FINAL VALIDATION
After setup:
Run entire status and available diagnostics.
Confirm the current branch and working-tree status remain intact.
Inspect all modified files.
Validate JSON configuration syntax where applicable.
Confirm existing Antigravity hooks and project hooks are preserved.
Confirm checkpoint auto-pushing remains disabled until authorized.
Run the relevant existing SENTINEL-X regression checks if any project files or application behavior were affected.
Confirm that no backend, frontend, database, or verifier behavior was unintentionally changed.
Verify that no secrets or generated runtime files were staged.
Do not commit or push anything.
If Entire cannot be installed or enabled because the current workspace is not a Git repository, provide the exact steps to open the real repository and continue there.
If a command is unavailable, use the installed CLI's own help and documentation instead of guessing.
FINAL REPORT
Return a concise, evidence-based report with:
Entire CLI installation status and version.
Repository root and current branch.
Antigravity integration status.
Git hook status and compatibility with existing hooks.
Checkpoint storage configuration.
Whether automatic checkpoint pushing remains disabled.
Privacy and secret-handling findings.
Files and settings changed.
Actual diagnostic commands and results.
Whether session capture was verified.
Whether commit-to-checkpoint linkage was fully tested or remains pending.
Exact next steps for me to test the integration in a new Antigravity session.
Any remaining blockers.
Do not claim success merely because the CLI is installed. Distinguish installation, repository enablement, agent-hook installation, session capture, and checkpoint linkage as separate verification states.
Do not commit, push, change branches, create remotes, or publish session data without explicit authorization.
BEGIN
Inspect the actual SENTINEL-X Git workspace, consult the official Entire CLI documentation, and integrate Entire with Antigravity safely. Preserve existing application functionality, Git history, privacy, and verification security. Implement what can be verified locally, and report anything requiring my explicit action.
</USER_REQUEST>

1: # SENTINEL-X — Entire CLI Integration Guide
2: 
3: This guide describes the integration of the official **Entire CLI** ([https://entire.io](https://entire.io), repository: [https://github.com/entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli)) with **SENTINEL-X** for AI-assisted development session provenance, Git checkpointing, and auditability.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. What Entire Does and Does Not Do
8: 
9: ### What Entire Does in SENTINEL-X
10: - **Developer Session Provenance**: Captures developer and AI agent interactions (prompts, tool calls, and diffs) during development in Antigravity.
11: - **Git Commit Association**: Automatically links captured agent sessions to standard Git commits via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers and isolated Git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/` backend).
12: - **Searchable Audit Trail**: Provides semantic and keyword search across historical agent sessions, commits, and reasoning paths (`entire search`, `entire checkpoint explain`).
13: - **Fail-Safe Secret Redaction**: Intercepts transcripts before persistence to redact credentials, tokens, and database connection strings using built-in multi-pass scanners (e.g., Betterleaks).
14: 
15: ### What Entire Does NOT Do
16: - **Not a Runtime Verifier**: Entire is strictly a development provenance tool. It does **not** evaluate patches, execute tests, or certify patch correctness.
17: - **Does Not Modify Runtime Pipeline**: Entire does **not** alter or replace `agent/planner.py`, `agent/generator.py`, `backend/workflow.py`, `backend/approvals.py`, `verification/patch_validator.py`, `verification/runner.py`, or `verification/evaluator.py`.
18: - **Not Verification Evidence**: Entire session history is developer telemetry, **not** proof that a patch passed the protected Docker sandbox test suite. It is not persisted in the SENTINEL-X verification database.
19: - **No Infallible Redaction**: Text scanners do not perform OCR on pasted screenshots or binary images. Any image pasted into an agent chat containing secrets will be saved unredacted in checkpoint assets.

23: ## 2. Prerequisites and Installation
24: 
25: ### Official CLI Installation (Linux / macOS / WSL)
26: The Entire CLI should be installed from the official stable release channel into the user directory (no root/sudo required):
27: 
28: ```bash
29: curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel stable
30: ```

32: The binary installs to `~/.local/bin/entire` along with `~/.local/bin/git-remote-entire`. Ensure `~/.local/bin` is in your `$PATH`:

34: ```bash
35: export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
36: entire version
37: ```

39: ### Git Repository Requirement

42: ```bash
43: # Verify Git root
44: git rev-parse --show-toplevel
45: ```

51: To enable Entire for Antigravity while keeping checkpoints and session data strictly **local-only** (preventing automatic remote publishing):
52: 
53: ```bash
54: entire enable --agent antigravity --skip-push-sessions
55: ```

57: ### What This Configures
58: 1. **Antigravity Hooks** (`.agents/hooks.json`):
59:    Registers hooks for Antigravity's lifecycle events:
60:    - `PreInvocation`: Invokes `entire hooks antigravity pre-invocation`
61:    - `PreToolUse`: Invokes `entire hooks antigravity pre-tool-use`
62:    - `Stop`: Invokes `entire hooks antigravity stop`

69:      },

72:          "type": "git-refs"

74:      }

85: 
86: ### Checkpoint Storage Models
87: - **Option A: Local-Only (Default Recommended)**:
88:   `push_sessions: false` ensures that session transcripts and checkpoint refs remain purely local on the developer workstation. No transcripts are pushed to upstream or origin Git remotes during normal `git push`.

### Category & Prize
